关键词: Global Magnitsky Human Rights Accountability Act
主要内容: On December 12, 2016, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctioned two Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) government officials, Evariste Boshab and Kalev Mutondo, under Executive Order 13413, as amended by Executive Order 13671. The sanctions were imposed due to their actions undermining democratic processes in the DRC, including delaying elections and suppressing political opposition. The Treasury stated that these actions threaten the long-term stability and prosperity of the country. The United Nations has also raised concerns about human rights violations and political repression in the DRC, including the arrest of opposition members and the use of torture. Boshab, the Deputy Prime Minister, was involved in delaying elections and influencing National Assembly members, while Mutondo, the General Administrator of the National Intelligence Agency, supported the neutralization of opposition demonstrations and extrajudicial arrests. On the same date, the U.S. Department of the Treasury sanctioned two Congolese government officials as part of broader efforts to address corruption and human rights abuses in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The officials were designated under the Global Magnitsky Human Rights Accountability Act, which allows the U.S. government to impose sanctions on individuals who have committed serious human rights violations or engaged in significant corruption. The Treasury Department stated that these actions are part of its commitment to promoting accountability and justice globally. The specific names and details of the officials were not disclosed in the initial announcement, but further information can be found by clicking the provided link.
